chunks: From al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ismail ibn Mahran, from Aiman ibn Mahraz, from Rufa'ah ibn Musa and Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Blessed is he who encounters the Qaim of my Ahl al-Bayt, following him before his rise, who takes the friends of his cause and disowns his enemies, and follows the guiding Imams who preceded him. Those are my companions, those of my love and affection, and the most honored of my nation with me.' Rufa'ah said: 'And the most honored of the creatures of Allah with me.'

key_terms.قَائِم: The Rising One (referring to Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of those blessed to follow the Qaim of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the concept of *al-intizar* (expectancy) as an active state of spiritual preparation rather than passive waiting, where believers align themselves with the Imam’s authority before his physical reappearance. It establishes a criterion for true faith by linking love for the Ahl al-Bayt with adherence to the preceding Imams, thereby ensuring continuity in religious leadership. The declaration that these individuals are 'most beloved to Allah' elevates the status of the occultation period as a crucial time for cultivating *walayah* (divine friendship).

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 466 - It is narrated from Fadhl bin Shazan from Ismail bin Mahran from Aiman bin Mahraz from Rufaa bin Musa and Muawiyah bin Wahab from His Eminence, Abu Abdullah Sadiq (a.s) that he said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) said: “Blessed be those, who are fortunate to live during the time of Qaim of my Ahle Bayt; those who would believe in him during his occultation and before his advent; who would love his friends and remain aloof from his enemies. Such people would be my closest ones and my friends on Judgment Day.” (According to the tradition of Rufaa) “And the most respected creatures of Allah in my view.”
